subject: general
question: The marked price of a laptop is ₹750. It sells with two successive discounts of 4% and 25%. An additional 25% discount is given on cash payment. What is the selling price (in ₹) of the laptop on cash payment?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective **Selling Price** = **Marked Price** × (100 − d₁)% × (100 − d₂)% × (100 − d₃)%

SP = 750 × (96/100) × (75/100) × (75/100)

SP = 750 × (24/25) × (3/4) × (3/4)

SP = 30 × 24 × 3 × 3 ÷ 16 = 720 × 9 ÷ 16 = 45 × 9 = 405

**∴ The correct answer is ₹405.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹750, **Discounts** = 4%, 25%, and an additional 25% for **cash payment**.
Formulas: SP = MP × (100 − D₁)% × (100 − D₂)% ...
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/765e7276895cd46818eb65feeb43950916cea2e4525f012ec9d2e39a5b141df0.png] 
⇒ Price after 1st discount = 750 × (96/100) = ₹720
⇒ Price after 2nd discount = 720 × (75/100) = 720 × 3/4 = ₹540
⇒ Price after 3rd (cash) discount = 540 × (75/100) = 540 × 3/4 = ₹405

**∴ The correct answer is ₹405.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When multiple discounts are applied one after another, the effective single discount is calculated as a + b − (ab ÷ 100).

Marked Price & Selling Price

Marked Price is the **labeled price**, and Selling Price is the final amount paid after deducting all applicable **discounts**.
